questions.question: How does frame-by-frame animation create the illusion of movement?
choices: A sequence of slightly changing images is shown in order
A single still image changes its file name
Audio is played backward
A camera lens zooms once

questions.question: What is a keyframe?
choices: The last image in every film
A frame marking an important pose or change in motion
A keyboard shortcut printed on screen
A sound effect synchronized to a scene

questions.question: Why use an animation timeline?
choices: To select a color palette only
To store copyright licenses
To arrange frames or events over time
To measure a character's height

questions.question: What is the purpose of an in-between frame?
choices: To replace the storyboard
To show a separate location
To remove timing from a scene
To create smoother motion between key poses

questions.question: How does changing frame rate affect animation?
choices: It changes how many frames display each second and can affect motion feel
It changes the drawing's aspect ratio
It sets the story's point of view
It guarantees realistic movement

questions.question: A bouncing ball looks weightless. What animation principle could improve it?
choices: Keep its shape and speed identical at all times
Show squash and stretch while preserving the ball's apparent volume
Remove the contact pose
Add unrelated background detail

questions.question: What is a storyboard used for?
choices: Exporting final audio levels
Choosing the screen brightness
Planning shots and story beats before producing the animation
Measuring the computer's memory

questions.question: Why is timing important in animation?
choices: It determines the file's copyright owner
It makes all motion realistic
It replaces the need for poses
It affects the perceived weight, speed, and emotion of an action

questions.question: What does an anticipation pose do?
choices: Prepares viewers for an upcoming action
Shows the action after it is finished
Keeps every character still
Hides the scene's setting

questions.question: Which sequence best communicates a character picking up a heavy box?
choices: Instantly move the box with no body change
Reach, brace, lift with effort, then settle under the weight
Move the box before the character reaches it
Keep the character still while the box floats

questions.question: What is onion-skinning useful for?
choices: Adding a permanent outline to every object
Editing a soundtrack
Seeing nearby frames faintly while drawing a new frame
Changing the camera angle automatically

questions.question: How can an animator make a walk cycle feel less mechanical?
choices: Use identical spacing for every body part
Remove contact with the ground
Add more frames without changing poses
Vary poses, timing, and weight shifts while keeping the cycle coherent

questions.question: Why should a scene's main action read clearly in silhouette?
choices: A clear shape helps viewers understand the pose and action
Silhouette proves the colors are accurate
It increases frame rate
It removes the need for timing

questions.question: What is easing in animation?
choices: A way to erase a frame
Gradually changing speed at the start or end of motion
A type of sound recording
A fixed camera distance

questions.question: What can a limited animation test reveal early?
choices: Whether the final film has a license
The exact audience size
Whether timing and poses communicate before detailed rendering
Whether the soundtrack is mixed

questions.question: If an object moves too far between frames, what may viewers perceive?
choices: A higher resolution
A new color space
A longer scene automatically
A sudden jump rather than smooth motion

questions.question: What is a looping cycle?
choices: A sequence designed to repeat smoothly
An animation that cannot be paused
A single title card
A sequence with no keyframes

questions.question: Why plan foreground, middle ground, and background layers?
choices: They guarantee a 3D camera
They can create depth and organize visual attention
They remove all overlap
They determine the dialogue

questions.question: What should be checked before exporting an animation?
choices: Only the project title
The computer wallpaper
Timing, playback, dimensions, and output format
The number of storyboard pages

questions.question: Why is feedback useful during animation production?
choices: Feedback always makes a project shorter
Feedback replaces planning
Feedback determines the frame rate
Viewers may notice unclear action or timing the creator overlooked
